LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 11.3.1 USE OF INTERROGATIVES

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.3: Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives, part of Strand 11 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: how much more..., when/who/why/what else with peers for example, who else attended the ceremony? how much more sugar was bought?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Grammar in Use 11.3.1 Use of Interrogatives together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn is inculcated as the learner learns to use interrogatives correctly.

• Collaboration is enhanced as the learner works collaboratively to construct questions using the target pattern.

Values:
Respect is cultivated when the learner uses digital devices to practice constructing questions with peers .

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion is reinforced as the learner engages in collaborative activities with peers to use interrogatives as

guided.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of interrogatives to similar concept learnt in Kiswahili.
